answer: Each loop of a spiral must be flown by the same sparrow that heard the opening whisper. A loop flown by another key does not count, and the whisper does not move to that key. An operator who splits one session into n keys still has the stamina of one sparrow, so the copies cannot divide the spiral among themselves. The unfinished loops stay unfinished. Waiting beside the route does not advance it, because a spiral grows only when that same sparrow flies the next loop.
